section: India and the WTO - agreements, ministerial conferences, public stockholding, fisheries subsidies, appellate body crisis
subsections: Other WTO agreements and Indian laws enacted

accepted.s:
With reference to public stockholding for food security in the WTO, consider the following statements:
1. The Bali Ministerial Conference of 2013 provided interim protection under a Peace Clause.
2. The Peace Clause prevents legal challenges even when food-security procurement exceeds the limits prescribed under the Agreement on Agriculture.
3. India is seeking a permanent solution to the issue.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Bali Peace Clause provides interim protection, while India seeks a permanent solution for its food-security procurement programmes.
accepted.tq: Combine three related features of a WTO arrangement and identify the option containing all correct statements.

accepted.s: Why does India's public stockholding issue under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture involve an outdated reference price?
o: Because the reference price is fixed by the World Bank every five years
Because MSP procurement for the National Food Security Act is calculated using a historical reference price
Because the reference price excludes all procurement by government agencies
Because the reference price is based on the international price of food imports in 2013
accepted.x: India argues that MSP procurement for the National Food Security Act is treated as an Amber Box subsidy using an outdated historical reference price.
accepted.tq: Test the precise technical detail behind a current policy controversy rather than its general description.

accepted.s: The negotiations on a permanent solution to the WTO public stockholding issue remained deadlocked at which Ministerial Conference?
o: MC11
MC10
MC13
MC14
accepted.x: The negotiations on a permanent solution to public stockholding remained deadlocked at the WTO's 14th Ministerial Conference.
accepted.tq: Use the conference-number trap by distinguishing the latest ministerial meeting from earlier WTO conferences.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT prohibited under the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies?
o: Subsidies for fishing on unregulated high seas
Subsidies connected with inland fishing
Subsidies for illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing
Subsidies for fishing in overfished stocks, unless rebuilding conditions apply
accepted.x: The Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies covers marine wild capture fishing and at-sea support. Aquaculture and inland fishing are exempt.
accepted.tq: Find the excluded activity rather than selecting one of the prohibited forms of fishing support.

accepted.s: The WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies applies primarily to which category of activity?
o: Only fishing undertaken within territorial waters
Only inland aquaculture operated by developing countries
Marine wild capture fishing and support provided at sea
All agricultural production connected with fisheries
accepted.x: The agreement covers marine wild capture fishing and at-sea support. It does not generally cover aquaculture or inland fishing.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the positive scope of an agreement from nearby excluded sectors.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding special treatment under the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies:
1. Developing countries and least-developed countries receive a two-year exemption in their exclusive economic zones.
2. The agreement provides for a Fish Fund to assist poorer members.
3. The exemption applies without any limitation to fishing on the high seas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The two-year exemption relates to fishing in the exclusive economic zones of developing countries and LDCs; it is not an unlimited high-seas exemption.
accepted.tq: Separate a limited territorial exemption from an incorrectly expanded high-seas exemption.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the recent status of the WTO Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies?
o: It was adopted in 2022 and entered into force in September 2025.
It was adopted in 2025 and entered into force in September 2026.
It was adopted in 2013 and entered into force in 2016.
It was adopted in 2020 but has not yet entered into force.
accepted.x: The agreement was adopted at MC12 in 2022 and entered into force in September 2025.
accepted.tq: Check both the adoption year and the later entry-into-force date.

accepted.s: The Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies is significant in WTO history because it is the first WTO agreement with which of the following objectives?
o: A military-security objective
A monetary-stability objective
A cultural-preservation objective
An environmental-sustainability objective
accepted.x: The Fisheries Subsidies Agreement is the WTO's first agreement with an environmental-sustainability objective.
accepted.tq: Identify the distinctive historical first associated with an agreement.

accepted.s: India became the 123rd WTO member to deposit its Instrument of Acceptance for the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies in:
o: June 2025
March 2026
September 2025
July 2026
accepted.x: India deposited its Instrument of Acceptance in July 2026, becoming the 123rd WTO member to do so.
accepted.tq: Combine a membership number with the exact month and year of a treaty action.

accepted.s: What was the immediate trade-related consequence of the lapse of the WTO e-commerce moratorium on 31 March 2026?
o: The moratorium was extended automatically for another decade.
All customs duties on physical goods were suspended.
The WTO prohibited digital imports by developing countries.
Developing countries lost tariff revenue on digital imports.
accepted.x: The lapse of the e-commerce moratorium exposed developing countries to the loss of tariff revenue on digital imports.
accepted.tq: Link the date of a policy change with its principal fiscal consequence.

accepted.s: The WTO e-commerce moratorium, which lapsed on 31 March 2026, had continued without such a lapse since:
accepted.x: The e-commerce moratorium lapsed for the first time since 1998.
accepted.tq: Test the “first time since” date rather than the more prominent lapse date.

accepted.s: The principal reason for the paralysis of the WTO Appellate Body is that:
o: The WTO Agreement on Dispute Settlement Understanding has expired.
India has refused to nominate appellate judges.
The European Union has withdrawn from the WTO dispute settlement system.
The United States has blocked appointments to the Appellate Body.
accepted.x: The United States has blocked appointments, leaving the Appellate Body non-functional since December 2019.
accepted.tq: Use the “who exercises the blocking role?” approach in an institutional question.

accepted.s: The WTO Appellate Body has been non-functional since:
o: December 2019
December 2018
December 2020
December 2017
accepted.x: The Appellate Body has been non-functional since December 2019 because appointments have been blocked.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the precise start date of an institutional crisis from nearby years.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Multi-Party Interim Appeal Arbitration Arrangement (MPIA)?
o: It is an EU-led stop-gap arrangement for appeals, and India has not joined it.
It is a compulsory arrangement to which all WTO members belong.
It is a fisheries agreement adopted by the WTO in 2022.
It is a permanent replacement for the WTO and is led by India.
accepted.x: The MPIA is an EU-led, 2020 stop-gap arrangement for appellate review during the Appellate Body crisis. India has not joined it.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between a temporary institutional arrangement and a permanent WTO body.

accepted.s: Which pair of WTO agreements is identified as the only two new agreements concluded in the last 30 years?
o: TRIPS and GATS
TFA and Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies
TRIMS and SPS
ITA and TBT
accepted.x: The Trade Facilitation Agreement and the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies are identified as the only two new WTO agreements concluded in the last 30 years.
accepted.tq: Start from the distinctive pair and eliminate agreements belonging to the original WTO package.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Agreement)
a. TRIPS
a. TRIMS
c. GATS
d. SPS/TBT
List-II (Subject)
i. Trade in services
ii. Minimum intellectual-property standards
iii. Investment measures affecting trade
iv. Food safety, plant and animal health, and technical standards
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: a–ii, b–iii, c–i, d–iv
a–iii, b–ii, c–iv, d–i
a–ii, b–i, c–iii, d–iv
a–iv, b–iii, c–i, d–ii
accepted.x: TRIPS concerns minimum IPR standards, TRIMS concerns trade-related investment measures, GATS concerns services, and SPS/TBT concern health and technical standards.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure pair TRIPS–IPR and complete the agreement-subject mapping.
accepted.sec: Other WTO agreements and Indian laws enacted

accepted.s: Which Indian law was enacted in 2005 to comply with the TRIPS requirement relating to product patents?
o: The Patents Act amendment of 2005
The Geographical Indications of Goods Act, 1999
The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006
The Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers’ Rights Act, 2001
accepted.x: India amended its Patents Act in 2005 to introduce product patents in accordance with TRIPS requirements.
accepted.tq: Match the legal enactment with the specific TRIPS-related compliance measure.
accepted.sec: Other WTO agreements and Indian laws enacted

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
1. Geographical Indications of Goods Act, 1999 — GI protection
2. PPV&FR Act, 2001 — plant varieties and farmers’ rights
3. Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 — food safety and standards
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: 1 only
1 and 2 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. These Indian enactments are associated with the relevant WTO-related compliance areas.
accepted.tq: Verify each law against its subject before selecting the all-correct combination.
accepted.sec: Other WTO agreements and Indian laws enacted

accepted.s: India's compliance with TRIMS involved the:
o: Adoption of zero duty on all agricultural products
Introduction of compulsory export subsidies for all industries
Withdrawal from all investment-related commitments
Phase-out of local-content conditions affecting trade
accepted.x: TRIMS concerns investment measures affecting trade, and India's compliance involved phasing out local-content conditions.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a trade-related investment obligation from tariff and export-subsidy measures.
accepted.sec: Other WTO agreements and Indian laws enacted

accepted.s: India's commitments under GATS are primarily associated with:
o: Zero duty on information-technology products
Liberalisation of trade in services
Regulation of illegal fishing subsidies
Protection of geographical indications only
accepted.x: GATS deals with trade in services, and India's compliance is reflected in its services-liberalisation commitments.
accepted.tq: Use the subject acronym to identify the corresponding area of WTO regulation.
accepted.sec: Other WTO agreements and Indian laws enacted

accepted.s: The Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 is associated with India's compliance in the area covered by:
o: SPS/TBT
TRIMS alone
TRIPS alone
The Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies
accepted.x: SPS/TBT cover food safety, plant and animal health, and technical standards. India's Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 is relevant to this area.
accepted.tq: Match an Indian statute with the WTO agreement category covering its subject.
accepted.sec: Other WTO agreements and Indian laws enacted

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Information Technology Agreement (ITA) is correct?
o: It concerns services liberalisation, and India has not signed it.
It concerns geographical indications, and India joined the Lisbon Agreement.
It concerns zero duty on IT products, and India is a signatory.
It concerns public stockholding, and India ratified it in 2016.
accepted.x: The ITA concerns zero duty on IT products, and India is a signatory to it.
accepted.tq: Separate the ITA from the similarly abbreviated trade agreements and identify its subject and Indian position.
accepted.sec: Other WTO agreements and Indian laws enacted

accepted.s: Which statement best describes India's position regarding the Lisbon Agreement on appellations?
o: India is a founding member but has suspended its membership.
India is a member and prefers it to TRIPS for GI protection.
India applies the Lisbon Agreement only to agricultural exports.
India is not a member and prefers TRIPS for GI protection.
accepted.x: India is not a member of the Lisbon Agreement on appellations and prefers to use TRIPS for geographical-indication protection.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two international frameworks dealing with geographical indications.
accepted.sec: Other WTO agreements and Indian laws enacted

accepted.s: The Doha Round of WTO negotiations is also known as the:
o: Technology Round
Investment Round
Environment Round
Development Round
accepted.x: The Doha Round, launched in 2001, is known as the Development Round and covers agriculture, NAMA and services.
accepted.tq: Recall the distinctive informal title associated with a negotiating round.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the status and principal areas of the Doha Round?
o: It began in 1995 and was completed on agriculture alone.
It began in 2001, covers agriculture, NAMA and services, and remains unfinished.
It began in 2013 and covers only trade facilitation.
It began in 2022 and covers only fisheries subsidies.
accepted.x: The Doha Round began in 2001, is concerned with agriculture, non-agricultural market access and services, and remains unfinished.
accepted.tq: Check the year, scope and completion status together to reject partially correct alternatives.

accepted.s: The G-33 was formed in 2003 during the Doha process primarily to address:
o: Only information-technology tariffs
Fisheries subsidies in developed countries
Only intellectual-property protection
Food security, special safeguard mechanisms and special products
accepted.x: The G-33 is a group of more than 40 developing countries, including India, focusing on food security, the Special Safeguard Mechanism and special products.
accepted.tq: Identify the negotiating group's agenda rather than its membership alone.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Doha Round — Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies only
G-33 — African Group, ACP and LDCs
G-90 — Food security and special products only
NAMA-11 — Developing countries negotiating on non-agricultural market access
accepted.x: NAMA-11 is a group of developing countries, including India, concerned with non-agricultural market access. The G-90 consists of the African Group, ACP countries and LDCs.
accepted.tq: Use group-purpose matching and reject the swapped descriptions of G-33, G-90 and NAMA-11.

accepted.s: The G-90 comprises which of the following groups?
o: The African Group, ACP countries and least-developed countries
NAMA-11 members and fisheries-exporting countries
The European Union, Japan and the United States
India, China, Brazil and other emerging economies only
accepted.x: The G-90 consists of the African Group, African, Caribbean and Pacific countries, and least-developed countries.
accepted.tq: Test the composition of a country group using the membership trap.

accepted.s: In the WTO dispute concerning India's National Solar Mission, the subject of contention was India's:
o: Ban on imports of agricultural products
Fisheries subsidy exemption
Public stockholding programme
Domestic-content requirement for solar cells
accepted.x: The US challenged the domestic-content requirement under India's National Solar Mission in dispute DS456.
accepted.tq: Match the dispute name with the specific domestic policy measure challenged.

accepted.s: What was the outcome of the WTO dispute DS456 concerning India's National Solar Mission?
o: India won in 2016
The United States withdrew the complaint before a panel report
India lost in 2016
The dispute was settled through the MPIA
accepted.x: India lost the solar-cells dispute, DS456, in 2016.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the dispute number and subject from the outcome and settlement mechanism.

accepted.s: The WTO dispute DS541 involving India concerned which set of measures?
o: MEIS, SEZ and EOU schemes
The National Solar Mission alone
Steel safeguards imposed by the United Kingdom
The National Food Security Act and MSP procurement
accepted.x: DS541 concerned India's export subsidies under the Merchandise Exports from India Scheme, SEZ and EOU schemes.
accepted.tq: Use the dispute number to identify the cluster of domestic schemes involved.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the WTO proceedings concerning India's export subsidies under DS541?
o: The panel ruled for India in 2019 and the United States appealed to the MPIA.
The panel ruled against India in 2019, after which the matter was appealed into the void.
The dispute was decided in India's favour in 2023 by the Appellate Body.
The dispute concerned only India's fisheries subsidies and was withdrawn in 2021.
accepted.x: The panel ruled against India in 2019 in DS541, and the appeal went into the void because of the Appellate Body crisis.
accepted.tq: Combine the panel year, adverse finding and distinctive phrase describing an ineffective appeal.

accepted.s: The WTO dispute brought by Brazil, Australia and Guatemala against India related to:
o: Steel safeguards imposed by the United Kingdom
Domestic content in solar cells
Tariffs on ICT products under the ITA
Cane prices and export subsidies
accepted.x: The sugar dispute involved India's cane pricing and export subsidies. The panel ruled against India in 2021, after which the matter was appealed.
accepted.tq: Match the complainant countries with the commodity and policy issue in dispute.

accepted.s: Which countries were involved in the WTO dispute concerning India's duties on phones and other ICT goods in relation to the ITA?
o: The United States, Canada and Mexico
Brazil, Australia and Guatemala
The European Union, Japan and Taiwan
China, South Africa and Indonesia
accepted.x: The ICT-tariff dispute was brought by the European Union, Japan and Taiwan and concerned duties on phones and ICT goods vis-à-vis the ITA.
accepted.tq: Identify the complainants in a trade dispute from a group of plausible country combinations.

accepted.s: The WTO panel ruled against India in the dispute concerning ICT tariffs in:
accepted.x: The panel ruled against India in the ICT-tariff dispute in 2023.
accepted.tq: Separate the years of the solar, export-subsidy, sugar and ICT disputes.

accepted.s: In May 2026, India raised the United Kingdom's steel safeguard at the WTO body known as the:
o: Dispute Settlement Body only
Council for Trade in Goods
Committee on Trade and Environment
Trade Policy Review Body
accepted.x: India raised the UK's steel safeguard at the Council for Trade in Goods in May 2026.
accepted.tq: Apply the “which WTO body handles goods-trade measures?” approach.

accepted.s: India's steel exports to the United Kingdom in 2025–26 were valued at approximately:
o: $389.4 million
$593.4 million
$893.4 million
$1,893.4 million
accepted.x: India's steel exports to the United Kingdom were valued at $893.4 million in 2025–26.
accepted.tq: Use ascending numerical options and distinguish the reported trade value from nearby figures.

accepted.s: The WTO's 14th Ministerial Conference held at Yaoundé in March 2026:
o: Adopted the Doha Development Round as completed
Issued a comprehensive declaration on all pending issues
Replaced the Appellate Body with the MPIA
Failed to issue a declaration
accepted.x: MC14, held at Yaoundé in March 2026, failed to issue a declaration.
accepted.tq: Test the outcome of the latest conference rather than its venue alone.

accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes India's concern regarding plurilateral initiatives such as the Investment Facilitation for Development and the E-Commerce Agreement?
o: They apply exclusively to agricultural subsidies and food security.
They may fragment the WTO system by moving away from consensus-based negotiations.
They would make the Appellate Body fully functional without appointments.
They would automatically abolish all WTO agreements.
accepted.x: India fears that plurilateral initiatives such as the IFD and E-Commerce Agreement may fragment the WTO by weakening the consensus-based multilateral approach.
accepted.tq: Apply the institutional principle of consensus to a contemporary negotiating debate.

accepted.s: Why are the WTO fisheries-subsidy rules of particular relevance to Andhra Pradesh?
o: They affect the interests of Andhra Pradesh's marine fisher folk, who have sought a fisher-centric approach.
They prohibit all fishing activity along the Andhra Pradesh coast.
They concern only software exports from Visakhapatnam.
They directly regulate only inland irrigation projects in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.x: The rules are relevant to Andhra Pradesh's marine fisher folk, and Indian fisher bodies have sought a fisher-centric approach to their implementation.
accepted.tq: Connect an international policy issue with its concrete regional stakeholder impact.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies is the first WTO agreement with an environmental objective.
2. The e-commerce moratorium lapsed for the first time since 1998.
3. India joined the Agreement on Fisheries Subsidies in July 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The Fisheries Subsidies Agreement is the WTO's first agreement with an environmental-sustainability objective, the moratorium lapsed for the first time since 1998, and India joined the fisheries agreement in July 2026.
accepted.tq: Combine separate current-affairs facts and check whether the comprehensive option is supported by all three.
